title: How do we multiply a whole number by tenths?
description: A whole number is multiplied by four tenths, three tenths and five hundredths, using tenths and hundredths as fractions, the same way as the pens in the book. A size check against whole numbers closes the working before the answers appear.
teaching_notes: One idea: a number of tenths or hundredths multiplies like a fraction, so multiply the top and keep ten or a hundred at the bottom. Watch for students who forget that the answer is still in tenths or hundredths.

source: Recall that a tenth is 0.1, a hundredth is 0.01, and so on. Find the following products in tenths, hundredths and so on: (a) 6 × 4 tenths (24 tenths) (b) 7 × 0.3 (c) 9 × 5 hundredths
video_script.why: The child has seen how a decimal price becomes a fraction over ten and now uses the same idea on tenths and hundredths.
video_script.substitution: the book's own three multiplications of a whole number by tenths and hundredths
video_script.anchor: Three multiplications from the book: six times four tenths, seven times zero point three, and nine times five hundredths
video_script.payoff_line: Each multiplication now has its answer.

final_answer.spoken: twenty four tenths, that is two point four. Twenty one tenths, that is two point one. Forty five hundredths, that is zero point four five

maths_rules: a tenth is 1/10 = 0.1 and a hundredth is 1/100 = 0.01
size check: 20 tenths = 2 and 30 tenths = 3, so 24 tenths and 21 tenths lie between 2 and 3; 50 hundredths = half, so 45 hundredths is a little less than half
video_script.design: One idea: tenths and hundredths multiply like fractions, as the pens did. Assumes tenths and hundredths. The three multiplications stay all video; the strip and the square stay through the ground; the decimals appear only on the answer beat.

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step one, solve the same way as the example in your book. Write four tenths as four over ten.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Multiply six by the top, four, and keep ten at the bottom.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>This gives twenty four over ten, that is twenty four tenths.

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step two, write zero point three as three over ten, which is three tenths.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Multiply seven by the top, three, and keep ten at the bottom.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>This gives twenty one over ten, that is twenty one tenths.

beats.colours: the top in the accent colour
narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step three, write five hundredths as five over one hundred.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Multiply nine by the top, five, and keep one hundred at the bottom.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>This gives forty five over one hundred, that is forty five hundredths.
